title: Two in five Indian family offices, UHNIs have engaged with crypto amid regulatory caution
summary: Around 41 percent of high-net-worth investors in India are delving into the world of cryptocurrencies and virtual digital assets, despite many only possessing a fundamental comprehension of this evolving landscape. Regulatory ambiguity poses a significant hurdle, with 59 percent expressing concerns. Investors frequently turn to informal channels, such as peer networks and social media, for insights on digital assets.

title: RBI net buyer of dollars for fourth straight month in September, data shows
summary: The Reserve Bank of India recorded net purchases of $6.94 billion in the foreign exchange market during September. It bought a total of $82.18 billion while selling $75.25 billion in currency transactions. Despite a decline in the rupee, capital inflows reached about $143 billion due to various measures. Indian equities have recently attracted investors, leading to a rise in the rupee's value.

SEBI eases KYC norms, centralises supplementary client data to simplify onboarding
summary: SEBI has revealed new measures aimed at simplifying the client onboarding process for investors. By centralising supplementary KYC details with KYC Registration Agencies, investors can avoid repetition. The revised framework will take effect on December 24, 2026, enhancing efficiency in data management. Intermediaries are instructed to report account closures promptly to maintain accurate KYC records. Investors are also advised against engaging with grey market premium figures for IPOs.

title: Sebi mulls early payout of up to 80% of sale proceeds to FPOs in commodity derivatives market
summary: Sebi introduced a proposal for an early pay-out framework designed to assist Farmer Producer Organisations. This framework would allow FPOs to access up to 80 percent of sale proceeds before contract expiry. The initiative aims to alleviate liquidity challenges by providing timely payments to farmers. Corporate trading members will offer this facility based on certain conditions and net worth requirements. Public comments on the proposal are invited until December 16.

title: RBI may opt for 25 bps rate hike as oil eases, inflation risks persist: Baroda BNP Paribas MF CIO
summary: The Reserve Bank of India is projected to implement a 0.25 percent interest rate hike in December. While decreasing crude oil prices could alleviate some inflation worries, many senior executives advocate for a measured strategy due to the prevailing economic climate. Nevertheless, concerns regarding food inflation and supply chain issues persist, adversely influencing overall forecasts.

title: US Treasury gains lift India bonds ahead of RBI meet
summary: On Wednesday, Indian government bonds rallied, influenced by a decrease in US Treasury yields. The benchmark 10-year bond yield fell to 7.1641%, marking a two-week low. The Indian rupee strengthened to its highest level for the fiscal year against the dollar. Overseas investors returned as net buyers of Indian debt, purchasing over 93 billion rupees. The Reserve Bank of India's upcoming decision will significantly affect market movements and trends.

title: Fed policymakers at odds over causes of high inflation
summary: US inflation is expected to increase again in October, with potential implications for Federal Reserve interest rate decisions. Economists predict the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index to reach 3.8% this month. Analysts are divided regarding whether inflation is caused by demand or supply shocks stemming from recent policies. Market forecasts suggest three more rate hikes, signaling ongoing concerns about rising prices.

title: Shapoor Mistry lobbied Modi twice for Tata Sons IPO as battle over listing intensifies
summary: Shapoor Mistry, the head of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, has reached out to Prime Minister Modi regarding the listing troubles faced by Tata Sons. He claims that Tata Trusts are obstructing the public offering for their own benefit and breaching regulations. Meanwhile, the Reserve Bank of India has pressured Tata Sons to meet listing necessities.

title: PhonePe resumes IPO process; targets February-March listing at $12-15 billion valuation
summary: PhonePe has resumed its initial public offering plans after deferring them due to market uncertainties. The company aims for a stock market listing valued between USD 12-15 billion in early 2024. It expects to raise approximately Rs 12,000-14,000 crore through an offer-for-sale. The digital payments firm has also reported significant revenue growth and is now profitable at the group level.
